Hi Frosty, dont apologise mate. The point I was making was this:

When those kinks of the CP where first made, in order for them to be FL's they needed to touch the blue zone, which they did.

So when we have the clean orders on the retrace we expect them to hit the red kinks and retrace back to a TG. In this case we only get small reactions and they never hit an opposing TG upon returning. Therefore, they are considered ignored. If they retraced to a MPL of the blue zone then blasted through the red areas, they would be considered used up as opposed to ignored.

Cheers

Well, then it's simple. An LS its an LS in a particular scale, but in most of the cases it is a FL in lower scale only. An ignored level is a a level which failed to create a symmetry. In your case, when price hit your LSK at QM1, why it didn't bounce back to point 2. If you wanted to trade at QM 1, and put a SL just above the LSK itself, your "first" maximum expectation would be a symmetry with your LSK, and the "second" maximum expectation would be to the point 2, so you can have a nice flag replicated to the right of it. Even if that symmetry didn't happened you could have a profitable trade from there because you still working in lower scales. But in higher scale, your QM 1 failed to hold price back to 2 so 1 it is an ignored level. Now you can trade it as a ignored level so A its a good iQM to trade from. Now, is it A a FL? Not in this scale but look on the second diagram on my picture. Its the same like yours, but i drawn some LTF things inside it. See how A breaks 3 and then, once it hit 4, which is the MPL of your bigger LSK, you can draw your FL A. So basically A it is a FL in lower scale and when price will retrace to A, you can try to fill in the first instance the flag A, and after that, maybe you will replicate again the flag between 3 and 4. Now, its your B a FL? In higher scale not, because it broke an unimportant level. (your LSK was just a to the 1-2 FL/LSK or whatever is it) but look in lower scale. Your LSK was a FL because it broke 5 which was a FL that holds price UP. When B broke your LSK and hit the next target (the point 6), you can draw the FL B. When price return to B you can try to trade at the MPL of it, hoping that in the first instance you can replicate the FL B, and after that you can try and replicate the flag 5-6 on the right side. And that's how history repeats itself. That's why forex is so hard, and that's why i think IF is a genius.
